claim: Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA) computes steering vectors as the mean difference in residual-stream activations between paired positive and negative behavioral examples, and adding these vectors at inference time reliably alters targeted model behavior while minimally degrading general capability.
stance_target: feasibility of activation-space intervention as a mechanism for correcting model behaviors such as miscalibrated verbal confidence
scope_conditions: Llama 2 Chat, multiple-choice behavioral datasets and open-ended generation tasks
quoted_support: CAA significantly alters model behavior, is effective over and on top of traditional methods like finetuning and system prompt design, and minimally reduces capabilities.

claim: Activation-space interpretation methods applied to CAA steering vectors provide insight into how high-level behavioral concepts are represented internally in LLMs, distinct from evaluation-protocol or metric-level analysis.
stance_target: the level at which calibration interventions operate (representational/mechanistic vs. measurement/protocol)
quoted_support: we gain deeper insights into CAA's mechanisms by employing various activation space interpretation methods. CAA accurately steers model outputs and sheds light on how high-level concepts are represented in Large Language Models (LLMs).
